title: Xdrip+ and G6 "stopped"
body:
Last night sensor just stopped. I also got a notification the the transmitter dropped in voltage but its only at 61 days. Sensor is 4 days old. Its trying to hard reset transmitter but is stuck. I see its "not connected" but nothing has changed on phone (Samsung Galaxy S20+). I'm lost if this is a BT problem, sensor problem, or transmitter problem. This happened a couple sensors ago and I had to replace (maybe the bad sensor) at day 6. I've attached a couple images. 
![Screenshot_20200531-113639_xDrip+](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25514585/83360142-de82e000-a333-11ea-9f08-a75dbb5577a0.jpg)
![Screenshot_20200531-113648_xDrip+](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25514585/83360143-df1b7680-a333-11ea-86f8-9ada153c62bf.jpg)
![Screenshot_20200531-113835_xDrip+](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25514585/83360144-dfb40d00-a333-11ea-9e71-781de3d9470b.jpg)

comments.body: Seems like your transmitter is "dead", battery voltage very low and obviously BT connection lost. After 61 days you should be able to claim the transmitter and receive a new one. Generally this kind of problem has been reported already a few times so you're not the only one. Call Dexcom. Sorry but that's the only answer that I can think of.
Thanks, I was leaning towards the same thing, but at only 61 days I was surprised. I wish they'd send two at a time if this was such a problem. I literally got a couple hours warning.

Ok, this is getting frustrating. I cannot appreciate enough the work that the developers of Xdrip are doing and I've always lived their work and it's been my choice to use. With that said, I wish their program was more user friendly. I cannot get to the root of whats going on. I have started a new transmitter and sensor and have not changed any setting in my phone. I am getting totally conflicting messages in xdrip. I started a session which it realized, and yet after the warm-up period I now get this? Was my transmitter ever really the problem or is it a bug in Xdrip?
![Screenshot_20200603-161809_xDrip+](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25514585/83698518-7bed4680-a5b6-11ea-850a-aa2c7c4945fc.jpg)

Everything I seem to do wants to revert to Xdrip thinking I have a G5 transmitter. Financially I'm well, and I'd send xdrip developers $1k a year just to give me something that works and I can get reasonable support from.
Sometimes the transmitter batteries don't last the full time. I think that is what has happened here.

@Schizm1 Would you please close this issue unless you still have this problem?
Thanks
